chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from some of our companions, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) lashed a man who married a woman during her postpartum bleeding period.

So it does not contradict the first report, because it is possible that he only established the punishment upon him because he had intercourse with her before her postpartum blood had completely exited, rather than establishing the punishment because he married her. And that which indicates this is that the narrator of this hadith, who is Abdullah ibn Sinan, narrated the like of the first report.

key_terms.خُرُوجِهَا: Her exiting/leaving (referring to the end of bleeding)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a woman during her postpartum period (nifas) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration to resolve apparent contradictions regarding the validity of marriage during *nifas* (postpartum bleeding). The report clarifies that Imam Ali’s administration of *hadd* (lashes) was likely due to illicit sexual intercourse occurring before the bleeding fully ceased, rather than invalidating the marriage contract itself, a distinction supported by the chain of transmission from Abdullah ibn Sinan.
